cf.title: Avoid redundant BitmapAnd with a clauseless partial index

input.subject: Avoid redundant BitmapAnd with a clauseless partial index

verdict_reasoning: No objection to the goal or the design survived at level 1. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-2, is a fixable level 2 point: message #1 gives no planning-time number for the added proof. The check mirrors one that choose_bitmap_and() already makes, and it rejects only plans whose BitmapAnd cannot remove rows. Confidence is low because only one message is visible and no planner committer has replied.

brief.title: Skip redundant BitmapAnd when a later index implies a partial index predicate
brief.problem: choose_bitmap_and() rejects a partial index whose predicate the already chosen quals imply, but misses the reverse order. When a clauseless partial index leads the AND group and a later index's quals imply its predicate, the BitmapAnd removes no rows but counts the predicate's selectivity twice. Users with a low random_page_cost can get this plan when the other index alone would be better.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds the mirror-image check to choose_bitmap_and() in indxpath.c. It rejects the combination only when the later index's quals imply the whole predicate, and only for plain IndexPaths, because find_indexpath_quals() flattens BitmapOr arms into one list. The patch adds regression tests in create_index.
user_visible_surface: Plan choice: some bitmap AND plans with a clauseless partial index are no longer chosen; no new syntax, GUC or API.
author_claims: In the repro, the BitmapAnd is estimated at about 15 rows against 2,000 actual.
With random_page_cost = 1.1 the planner picks the BitmapAnd, including on the outer side of a nested-loop semi join.
With the default random_page_cost the plan does not change.
The BitmapAnd cannot remove any rows in this case.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. Nobody has replied, and the CommitFest entry is in Needs review.
unclear: The proposal does not say whether a partly implied predicate, or a BitmapOr arm, still gets the double-counted estimate.
The author gives no planning-time cost for the extra predicate proof.
The material does not show the repro schema or the plans before and after the patch.
The proposal does not say whether it targets back branches.

objections.title: Extra predicate proofs add planning cost for every partial-index query
objections.failure_scenario: An OLTP schema has several partial indexes on one table and short queries that plan each time. After the change, choose_bitmap_and() runs another predicate_implied_by() proof for candidate pairs, and planning time goes up for every such query, including those whose plan never changes. The cost appears only after upgrade, in latency numbers.
objections.argument: The patch adds a second implication proof in a loop that already does one, and it runs for every query with a clauseless partial index among the bitmap candidates. Message #1 gives no planning-time measurement, and the brief marks this as unknown. The plan gain is limited to setups with a low random_page_cost, while the proof cost falls on every query with this index shape.
objections.author_must_show: What is the planning-time cost of the added proof on a table with many partial indexes and many bitmap candidates, measured on a query whose plan does not change?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 gives no planning-time number, so the request for one stands. The cost is narrower than stated: the new proof runs only when a clauseless partial index leads the AND group, in a loop that already runs predicate_implied_by().

refuted.title: Narrow ordering special case leaves the double-counted estimate elsewhere
refuted.failure_scenario: A user has a partial index whose predicate is only partly implied, or is implied through a BitmapOr arm. The planner still counts the predicate's selectivity twice and picks the same kind of bad BitmapAnd. The user reports a near-identical bug, and a second patch in choose_bitmap_and() is needed for it.
refuted.argument: The commit message excludes BitmapOr arms and partial implication on purpose, so the fix covers one shape of a general estimation error. The proposal does not say whether the double count could be removed where selectivity is computed, which would cover every order and arm shape. In [P1], a different indxpath.c fix was not accepted partly because it fixed one path shape and left estimates unchanged. A committer would likely ask whether this mirror-image check is the general fix or another local guard.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is a mirror-image check in choose_bitmap_and() better than removing the double-counted predicate selectivity where bitmap AND selectivity is computed?

precedents_retrieved.title: bitmap cost should account for correlated indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes cost_bitmap_heap_scan use the index correlation statistic, as cost_index already does, so a correlated bitmap scan is estimated to fetch fewer pages and read them more sequentially. It also adds correlation rules for BitmapAnd and BitmapOr nodes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: After Heikki Linnakangas marked the patch Ready for Committer, Tom Lane objected that index correlation does not show whether a given scan reads tightly clumped data, and that the patch ignores the index condition. He also found the BitmapAnd and BitmapOr correlation rules too optimistic and the new cost equations unsupported by real examples. The author did not reply, and the entry was returned with feedback after more than a month in Waiting on Author.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
Reverted commit(s): Ignore BRIN indexes when checking for HOT udpates; Move test for BRIN HOT behavior to stats.sql
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 5753d4ee32 and fe60b67250 that modified HOT to
ignore BRIN indexes. The commit message for 5753d4ee32 claims that:

    When determining whether an index update may be skipped by using
    HOT, we can ignore attributes indexed only by BRIN indexes. There
    are no index pointers to individual tuples in BRIN, and the page
    range summary will be updated anyway as it relies on visibility
    info.

This is partially incorrect - it's true BRIN indexes don't point to
individual tuples, so HOT chains are not an issue, but the visibitlity
info is not sufficient to keep the index up to date. This can easily
result in corrupted indexes, as demonstrated in the hackers thread.

This does not mean relaxing the HOT restrictions for BRIN is a lost
cause, but it needs to handle the two aspects (allowing HOT chains and
updating the page range summaries) as separate. But that requires a
major changes, and it's too late for that in the current dev cycle.

precedents_retrieved.title: Predicate locking in SP-Gist index
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds explicit predicate locking to the SP-GiST index access method for serializable isolation. It takes predicate locks only on leaf pages and copies a lock from the original page to the new page during a page split.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Alexander Korotkov found that locking only leaf pages misses conflicts. When choose returns spgAddNode, the insert adds a new branch that earlier scans could have used, so internal pages need predicate locks too. He also found that the patch moves predicate locks only when doPickSplit() allocates a new leaf page, but SP-GiST can move items to free space on another busy page. Daniel Gustafsson returned the patch based on this review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
And this new branch could probably be used by scans we
made in the past.  Therefore, you need to do predicate locking for internal
pages too in order to detect all the possible conflicts.

precedents_retrieved.title: Decoupling our alignment assumptions about int64 and double
precedents_retrieved.summary: Split TYPALIGN_DOUBLE into three alignment codes: TYPALIGN_DOUBLE for float8 only, TYPALIGN_INT64 ('l') for 64-bit integer types and pointers, and TYPALIGN_MAX for composite types. This would end the assumption that ALIGNOF_DOUBLE is the maximum alignment, which breaks on AIX, where alignof(int64) = 8 but alignof(double) = 4.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it. The change alters user-table row layout on platforms where int64 and double alignment differ, so it breaks pg_upgrade there, and binary-compatible casts declared with "like int8" failed dump and reload. The deciding problem was extensions: an existing type's typalign cannot be changed without table rewrites, and a type created with "LIKE int8" would get 'l' or 'd' depending on whether it was pg_upgraded or installed fresh, so the two codes would end up assigned at random. Only the att_align_nominal() refactoring from the series was committed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Perhaps we could have got away with such a change in the pre-pg_upgrade era, but I think we cannot now.

precedents_retrieved.title: In bitmap scan explain node show how many relevant heap pages were not examined
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an "unfetched" count under "Heap Blocks" in EXPLAIN ANALYZE for Bitmap Heap Scan, next to "exact" and "lossy", for heap pages that the visibility map let the bitmap-only scan skip. The author also suggested renaming the node to "Bitmap Only Heap Scan" but did not implement it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane questioned the need for the counter, because index-only scans report only "Heap Fetches: n" and get no comparable data. He held that the two should be consistent and that the lack of complaints about index-only scans suggests users do not need the information. Amit Kapila marked the entry Returned with Feedback at the end of the commitfest, without further opinions.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
Reverted commit(s): Fix index-only scan plans when not all index columns can be returned.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 4ace45677 failed to fix the problem fully, because the
same issue of attempting to fetch a non-returnable index column
can occur when rechecking the indexqual after using a lossy index
operator.  Moreover, it broke EXPLAIN for such indexquals (which
indicates a gap in our test cases :-().

Revert the code changes of 4ace45677 in favor of adding a new field
to struct IndexOnlyScan, containing a version of the indexqual that
can be executed against the index-returned tuple without using any
non-returnable columns.  (The restrictions imposed by check_index_only
guarantee this is possible, although we may have to recompute indexed
expressions.)  Support construction of that during setrefs.c
processing by marking IndexOnlyScan.indextlist entries as resjunk
if they can't be returned, rather than removing them entirely.
(We could alternatively require setrefs.c to look up the IndexOptInfo
again, but abusing resjunk this way seems like a reasonably safe way
to avoid needing to do that.)

This solution isn't great from an API-stability standpoint: if there
are any extensions out there that build IndexOnlyScan structs directly,
they'll be broken in the next minor releases.  However, only a very
invasive extension would be likely to do such a thing.  There's no
change in the Path representation, so typical planner extensions
shouldn't have a problem.

As before, back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove redundant NULL check in clause_selectivity_ext()
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Remove redundant NULL check in clause_selectivity_ext()
Threads: Remove redundant NULL check in clause_selectivity_ext() function

roaster_notes.note: Neither precedent's reason applies here. The patch mirrors an existing check in choose_bitmap_and(), and the plans it rejects cannot remove rows, so P4's lost-plan problem does not arise; the thread cites no earlier discussion.

The proposal adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, dump state or client-visible output. It changes plan choice only in a case where the BitmapAnd cannot remove rows, by mirroring a check choose_bitmap_and() already makes. If it were back-patched, plans would change in a minor release, but the proposal does not say it targets back branches, so I raise no objection on that.

The proposal changes only plan choice in choose_bitmap_and() in indxpath.c, plus regression tests. It adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or extension API state, so this angle has nothing to object to. Possible plan changes after a minor upgrade belong to the planner angle.

The patch only changes which bitmap index paths choose_bitmap_and() combines. It adds no new privilege, object, setting or function, and it exposes no data or state. Predicate proofs use only immutable expressions, so no user-controlled code runs during planning. The proposal therefore has no security or privilege aspect to object to.
Two fixable design points. Committability: no planner committer has replied yet. The change is small and stays in one function, so the maintenance cost after commit is low.

From this angle the proposal has no existing substitute. It extends the existing redundancy check in choose_bitmap_and() to the reverse order and adds no second mechanism. Per-query workarounds such as enable_bitmapscan = off or the pg_hint_plan extension can avoid the bad plan in a known query, but they do not fix the double-counted selectivity estimate, and no hook lets an extension change choose_bitmap_and().

No demand objection applies. The patch adds the mirror-image of an existing check in choose_bitmap_and() for a misestimate that removes no rows, and random_page_cost = 1.1 is a common setting on SSD-backed systems. The material has only a synthetic repro and no field report, and the planning-time cost is unmeasured, but both are design questions for other angles.
